recentItems.description:
Police are appealing to the public to come forward with any information that could help identify the perpetrators behind the killings of women in Ekurhuleni. So far, six bodies have been discovered.

recentItems.title: 6th female body discovered in Kwa-Thema could be linked to the five murders in Kempton Park #fyp
recentItems.description:
The South African Police Service are not ruling out the possibility that the sixth female body that was discovered in Kwa-Thema in Ekurhuleni could be linked to the other five murders that took place in Kempton Park.

recentItems.title: Ekurhuleni Deaths | Community involvement crucial to help fight crime - Gen. Fred Kekana
recentItems.description:
Mothers and community members in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, say they are increasingly concerned about the safety of young women and girls amid a growing number of unexplained killings in the metro. Police have returned to the latest crime scene in KwaThema, Springs, to gather evidence and determine whether the cases are linked. 

For the latest on the investigation and efforts to determine whether the cases are linked, we are joined in studio by Gauteng SAPS Acting Provincial Commissioner, Major General Fred Kekana.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Sixth body found: Dr Saths Cooper weighs in on psychological factors behind violent offending
recentItems.description:
A woman's body has reportedly been discovered in Kwa-Thema, Springs, in Ekurhuleni.

The latest discovery brings to six the number of women whose bodies have been found across Ekurhuleni over the past two months.

The repeated discoveries have raised concerns about possible links between the cases, although authorities have not confirmed that they are connected.

For more on the psychological factors behind violent offending and what may drive serial offending, we speak to clinical psychologist Saths Cooper.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Refugee Relocation | Buses arrive to move refugees from Durban streets
recentItems.description:
Buses have arrived in Durban to transport refugees who have been living on the streets outside a Home Affairs refugee centre for the past four months.

Officials have verified the documentation of about 300 foreign nationals, who are now expected to be transported to the Lindela Repatriation Centre in Krugersdorp.

For the latest on the relocation process and the refugees' situation, we touch down to SABC News reporter Mlondi Radebe in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Suspended Crime Intelligence police officer Fannie Nkosi back in court - Chriselda Lewis reports
recentItems.description:
Suspended Crime Intelligence Police Officer, Fannie Nkosi is back in the Pretoria Regional Court for the disclosure of dockets. 

His two consolidated cases were transferred to the Regional Court after the National Prosecuting Authority secured a centralisation certificate to have the two cases heard together. 

Nkosi has been in custody since his arrest in April. SABC News Reporter, Chriselda Lewis is in court.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Key witness expected to testify in Matlala and co-accused trial - Neria Hlakotsa reports
recentItems.description:
A key witness for the defence is expected to take the stand in the attempted murder trial of Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala and four others, when it resumes at the High Court in Johannesburg.

Matlala is accused of orchestrating three failed assassination attempts targeting his former girlfriend Tebogo Thobejane, businessman Joe Sibanyoni, and music producer Seunkie Mokubung, popularly known as DJ Vettys. 

The alleged assassination attempts occurred between August 2022 and January 2024.

For more we cross to our reporter Neria Hlakotsa.
